review.tagline: CLI that packs a repository into one XML, Markdown or JSON file for LLMs
review.summary: Repomix is a Node.js CLI that combines a repository's files into a single XML, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file with a directory tree and per-file token counts. It respects .gitignore, .ignore and .repomixignore, runs Secretlint to leave out files with credentials, and can compress code with Tree-sitter. It can also pack remote repos, take file lists via stdin, and add git logs or diffs.
review.audience: Developers feeding whole codebases into ChatGPT, Claude or other LLMs
strengths: One command (npx repomix) packs a repo; no install or config required
--compress uses Tree-sitter to cut token count while keeping code structure
Supports --remote repos, --stdin file lists, glob include/ignore, and git logs or diffs
Secretlint check leaves files matching known credential formats out of the output
weaknesses: Produces a static file to paste into an AI tool; it does not edit code itself
Large repos can exceed model context limits even with compression
Browser and VSCode integrations are separate; the VSCode one is community-maintained
Secret detection covers known credential formats only, so output still needs review
needs: Models: XML output, Markdown output, JSON output, Plain text output
